Ṛṣabha
grammarian. Q. in Hemacandra's Nyāsa on his Bṛhadvṛtti. See Ind. Ant.

Ṛṣabha
son of Sudhanvan an. grandson of Aṅgiras, a sage connected with Āyurveda. Q. in Āyurveda kā itihās, p. 60. [Page035-b]

Ṛṣabhagāna
Sv. (?) Rep. Raj. & C. I. p. 3.

Ṛṣabhagītā
M. Bhārata, Rājadharma, chs. 125-8, Chitrasala Press edn.; on Āśā; dialogue between sage Ṛṣabha an. King Sumitra; same chs. in Kumbhakonam edn., but not called Gītā there.

Ṛṣabhagītā
teachings of Ṛṣabha, son of Nābhi, an. a. incarnation of Viṣṇu. Hpr.

Ṛṣabhacarita(tra)(dharmopadeśaśata)
Jain. Pkt. by Bhuvanatuṅga. Pattan I. p. 62 (inc.).

Ṛṣabhacaityavandana
Jain. composed a. a Bhaktāmara-pādapūrtikāvya on the victory of Jñānavimalasūri (18th century). Q. in “Jñānavimala sūrīśvara num Ādarśa Jīvanacaritra” of Kanakavimala. See Jaina Sid. Bhās. III. iii. p. 109.

Ṛṣabhamahimnastotra
Jain. a pāda-pūrti-kāvya by Ratnaśekharasūri based on the Śivamahimnasstava. See Jaina Sid. Bhas. III. iii. p. 111.
Pt.. Jaina stotra tathā stavanasaṅgraha, artha sahita. 1907 A. D.

Ṛṣabhādeśa(ºbhopadeśa)
from the Brahmottarakhaṇḍa. Bikaner 1316.
See Venk. edn. of Brahmottarakhaṇḍa, chs. 10-11, an. also 12-14; chs. 10-11 contain two courses of teachings by the Śivayogin named Ṛṣabha an. ch. 11 is called Ṛṣabhopadeśa in col.

Ṛṣabhopadeśana
